facts.statement: Fossils of Baotianmansaurus were discovered in the Late Cretaceous Gaogou Formation of Henan Province, China.
facts.quote: Its fossils were discovered in the Late Cretaceous Gaogou Formation of Henan Province, China.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Baotianmansaurus, designated 41HIII-0200, is stored at the Henan Geological Museum in Zhengzhou.
facts.quote: The holotype, and only known specimen of Baotianmansaurus was given the designation 41HIII-0200 and is stored at the Henan Geological Museum in Zhengzhou.

facts.statement: Baotianmansaurus was named in April 2009 by a research team led by Zhang Xingliao.
facts.quote: It was described and given a name in April 2009 by a team of researchers including Zhang Xingliao, Lü Junchang, Xu Li, Li Jinhua, Hu Weiyong, Jia Songhai, Ji Qiang, and Zhang Chengjun

facts.statement: The genus name Baotianmansaurus combines the Baotianman Nature Reserve with the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The genus was named "Baotianmansaurus" after the Baotianman Nature Reserve and the traditional Greek word saûros (σαῦρος), Latinized as saurus, meaning "lizard".

facts.statement: Baotianmansaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 75 million years ago in the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 75 millones de años durante el Campaniense

facts.statement: Researchers estimated Baotianmansaurus to be about 22.5 meters long, 5.3 meters tall at the shoulder, and weigh 21 tons.
facts.quote: Rubén Molina-Pérez and Asier Larramendi estimated the full size of Baotianmansaurus at about 22.5 m long, 5.3 m tall at the shoulder, and weighing 21 t

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Baotianmansaurus to be 20 meters long and weigh 15 tons.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul published a slightly smaller estimate of 20 m long and weighing 15 t.

facts.statement: Baotianmansaurus is distinguished by unique features including spongy back vertebrae, short neural spines, apneumatic ribs, and amphicoelous caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Baotianmansaurus can be distinguished from all other sauropods by the presence of the following autapomorphies: a spongy character of the back vertebrae, short neural spines on the vertebrae of the middle back, a developed system of 11 e on the vertebrae, apneumatic ribs, amphicoelous caudal vertebrae that are shorter than they are wide, and several specific features of the vertebral laminae.

facts.statement: The exact classification of Baotianmansaurus has been controversial since its description.
facts.quote: The exact affinities of Baotianmansaurus have been controversial since it was first described.

facts.statement: A 2019 study suggested a close relationship between Baotianmansaurus, Dongyangosaurus, and Diamantinasauria.
facts.quote: A 2019 examination of sauropods from the Tendaguru Formation found a close relationship between Baotianmansaurus, Dongyangosaurus, and the Diamantinasauria.

facts.statement: Recent analyses place Baotianmansaurus either as a non-titanosaur somphospondylian or as a basal titanosaur.
facts.quote: More recent analyses using various datasets have recovered Baotianmansaurus as either a non-titanosaur somphospondylian closely related to Huanghetitan or a basal member of Titanosauria closely related to Andesaurus and Abdarainurus.

facts.statement: Baotianmansaurus is likely closely related to Opisthocoelicaudia and Dongyangosaurus.
facts.quote: Probablemente este cercanamente emparentado con Opisthocoelicaudia y Dongyangosaurus.

facts.statement: The time range for Baotianmansaurus is estimated from 93.9 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Campanian (93.9 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Baotianmansaurus is an extinct genus of somphospondylian sauropod.
rejected.quote: Baotianmansaurus is an extinct genus of somphospondylian sauropod.
